h1: Check in Phureeya Ville — a mountain retreat in Pong Nam Ron where you wake up to mist and cool air
intro: Picture this: you open your villa's terrace door in the early morning and find a thin veil of mist drifting around the peaks all around you, the air cool enough to reach for a jacket, your first hot coffee in hand — Check in Phureeya Ville, or as locals call it, Phureeya Ville, is a small mountain villa resort in Thap Sai, Pong Nam Ron, Chanthaburi · it's a villa-style stay of around 8 houses spread across grounds ringed by 360-degree mountain views · what many people talk about is the quiet, the privacy, and the cool, comfortable air almost year-round, ideal for anyone who really wants to escape the city · scored 8.3 from 61 reviews — a small stay that sells atmosphere more than luxury.

body.html: Who Check in Phureeya Ville suits — to put it as simply as possible, Phureeya Ville is for people who want to "escape the city and really be among the mountains" · it isn't a luxury hotel in downtown Chanthaburi, and it isn't a beachfront resort with every facility on hand · it's a small, family-run villa resort set in the mountains of Thap Sai, Pong Nam Ron, the eastern part of Chanthaburi known for cool air and mist · there are around 8 villas spread across the grounds, accommodating roughly 30 guests when full · each one has a balcony or terrace where you can sit and take in the mountains that surround you on all sides, a full 360 degrees · from real reviews and the property's own information, the people who fit here are couples wanting a quiet, private stay, families bringing kids and grandparents for a change of scenery, and groups of friends who want to book out a villa and sit around together in the cool air · on the flip side, if you're expecting a hotel with a big swimming pool, a gym, a full-service spa, or you want to walk out the door and reach malls and restaurants on foot, this may not be your answer, because the charm of Phureeya Ville lies in the quiet and the nature around it rather than city-style convenience · in plain terms, it's a stay that sells "atmosphere and quiet" above all, at a price you can manage — which is exactly what most people heading to Pong Nam Ron and Khao Soi Dao are after.

Location and getting there — Phureeya Ville sits at 12/12 Moo 6, Thap Sai, Pong Nam Ron, Chanthaburi · it's about 35–40 km from downtown Chanthaburi, roughly a 40–50 min drive depending on road conditions and time of day · Pong Nam Ron is an eastern border district next to Pailin Province in Cambodia, so it's a mountain area with cool air and mist through much of the year · getting here works best for people driving themselves, because the property sits out in nature without convenient public transport running past like in town · the good news is there's free parking on the grounds, plus a pickup service (for an extra charge) for those not driving in · one thing to brace for: the final stretch of road into the resort climbs uphill and passes through villages and fruit orchards, and some sections may be narrow or winding — drive carefully, especially at night or during rain when mist can roll in · we'd suggest turning on your GPS and calling the property ahead for directions, since it's a small stay in a mountain area where the map pin can be a little off · once you arrive, it's worth the drive, because you get an atmosphere you simply can't find in town.

"The drive up was a bit tiring, but the moment we reached the place the tiredness disappeared. The mountain views all around are gorgeous, and in the morning a thin mist settles in and the air is lovely and cool. I sat sipping coffee on the terrace all morning — genuinely quiet and peaceful, perfect for anyone who wants to relax."

Villa types and decor — Phureeya Ville is a stay of standalone villas, not a block of hotel rooms · according to the property there are around 8 villas, and some sources note a mix of single-storey and two-storey houses, each designed with a sitting area and a balcony/terrace for taking in the mountain views · the decor is a simple, warm-toned resort style that blends with the surrounding nature rather than going for luxury · the in-room amenities listed include air conditioning, satellite TV, a fridge, and a private bathroom with a shower and hot water, plus toiletries · what many people like is that the villas are separate buildings, which gives a strong sense of privacy and suits couples or a whole family booking out a place together · to be honest, since this is a small stay in a mountain area, the condition and finish of each villa may not be identical — some can look plain in the way of an upcountry resort · anyone who cares especially about the view or villa size should ask and spell out their needs when booking — which villa, how many people, and which direction you want to face — because booking directly with a small place like this tends to be flexible and open to discussing the details.

Facilities and activities — because it's a small mountain resort, the facilities at Phureeya Ville keep things simple but cover what you need to relax · there's a 24-hour front desk, free parking, and a restaurant and terrace on the grounds · the standout feature is the 360-degree mountain views and the mist, which act like a natural amenity you can sit and enjoy all day without going anywhere · for families with kids, several reviews mention the children having fun running around the garden, and the property has at times offered activities like a bonfire and karaoke, giving groups of friends or families who book out a villa a sociable atmosphere · some sources note a massage service, plus hiking and cycling in the nearby area, and pets are welcome at no extra charge — a plus for anyone who doesn't want to leave their dog or cat at home · important to know: this property has no swimming pool, and the Wi-Fi information isn't clear — some sources say there's free Wi-Fi, others say there isn't · to be safe, if you need stable internet or a strong mobile signal, ask the property directly before booking, because a signal in a mountain area like this may not be as strong as in town — but for many people, getting to switch off from screens for a couple of days is itself one of the upsides of staying here.

Food and cafe — Phureeya Ville has an on-site restaurant and cafe, which is a point guests praise · the property highlights quality coffee served against the mountain views, which makes sipping a morning coffee on the terrace one of the things guests enjoy most · for food, it serves Thai and Asian dishes, with breakfast available plus room service according to the listed information · real reviews say the food is tasty and reasonably priced, which matters a lot for a stay this far from town, since most guests can't easily drive out to find a restaurant for every meal · our honest tip: because this is a small mountain stay a fair distance from convenience stores and restaurants in the district town, ask the property about meals ahead of time — when the kitchen is open, whether you need to order in advance, and whether there are options for vegetarians or guests with dietary restrictions · plan well and you'll eat well without having to head far out to find food on a mountain night.

Service — the strength of a small, family-run place like Phureeya Ville is the warm, friendly care · from real reviews, many guests praise the welcome and the attentive service, which makes it feel more like staying at a relative's house than at a hotel · there's a 24-hour front desk, and the owner/team are good at chatting and giving recommendations on attractions, routes, and meals · because it's a small property, most communication happens by phone or Line directly, which makes it more flexible to adjust details than booking through a big system · one honest note: the service standard at a small place like this depends on the time and the number of guests — come during a long holiday when it's busy and the attention may not be as thorough as on a quieter weekday · overall, service is still a point that leaves people impressed and that they speak about warmly.

Voices from real reviews (praise and gripes) — gathered from booking and review platforms for Chanthaburi stays, the overall picture is fairly consistent · on the praise side: the mountain views and mist are gorgeous, especially in the morning; the air is cool and comfortable; the atmosphere is quiet and private; the standalone villas suit families and groups of friends; the food is tasty and the coffee is good, all reasonably priced; the kids have fun playing in the garden; and the staff are friendly · it scored 8.3 from 61 reviews, which is good for a small stay in a remote area · on the watch-out side: the thing that comes up is getting there — it's far from town and the final stretch climbs uphill, so drive yourself and take care at night · next is the simple facilities in the style of an upcountry resort, no swimming pool, and internet/mobile signal that may not be as strong as in town, plus the condition and details of the villas that may not be identical across all of them · these gripes are normal for a mountain stay that sells nature rather than being problems that put people off returning — set your expectations right from the start and you'll have a great trip.

"We came as a family and booked out a villa, and the kids had a blast running around the garden. In the evening we all sat around eating and chatting in the cool air · the only downside was the weak mobile signal, but that turned out to be a good thing because everyone put their phones down and actually talked to each other."

Price and value — Phureeya Ville sits in the budget-to-mid range for a Pong Nam Ron trip · villa rates often start around ฿1,200 a night and up, climbing with villa size, the number of guests, and the season — especially the cool season (November–February), the high season for mountain trips on this side, when prices and demand run higher than usual · since it's a small place that isn't fully listed on every platform, the most accurate price is best checked with the property directly by phone or Line · compared with other mountain-view stays around Pong Nam Ron and Khao Soi Dao, Phureeya Ville feels good value for atmosphere and privacy, especially if you come as a group or family and book out a whole villa, because you get plenty of private space, mountain views all around, and food and coffee at the property without driving far · if you measure value by a swimming pool or luxury facilities, this isn't it — but if you measure it by "a quiet rest in nature on a budget you can manage," it suits that crowd well.

What to know before booking — a few things help make the stay smoother · one, a small place like this has limited availability, especially in the cool season and on long holidays, so book ahead and confirm directly with the property to be safe · two, ask about the current price, villa size, and how many people each villa holds before transferring a deposit, since details can change by season · three, plan your travel — drive yourself, fill the tank before heading into the mountain area, and allow extra time if you'll arrive in the evening, since the road winds and mist can roll in · four, ask about meals and kitchen hours ahead of time, since you're far from outside restaurants · five, if you're bringing a pet, let the property know first, and if you need internet or mobile signal, check with them how well it's covered · six, pack warm clothes if you come in the cool season, because the air in the mountains is far cooler than in town, especially from night into the early morning.

Verdict — from real reviews and the information we gathered, Check in Phureeya Ville (Phureeya Ville) is the best fit for anyone who wants to escape the city for a quiet, private rest in the mountains on a budget they can manage · the 360-degree mountain views, morning mist, cool comfortable air, standalone villas, on-site food and coffee, and friendly care make it a strong choice for couples, families, and groups of friends heading to Pong Nam Ron and Khao Soi Dao · if you're after a luxury hotel with a swimming pool, a spa, and a location within walking distance of shops in town, this isn't your answer, and you'd be better off considering a hotel in downtown Chanthaburi · but for a trip where you want nature, quiet, and cool air at a friendly price — Phureeya Ville is a mountain retreat that meets that need squarely, as long as you drive yourself and set your expectations right from the start.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Check in Phureeya Ville (Phureeya Ville)

faq.q: Where is Check in Phureeya Ville, and how do you get there?
faq.a: The property is at 12/12 Moo 6, Thap Sai, Pong Nam Ron, Chanthaburi, in the mountains on the eastern side of Chanthaburi · it's about 35–40 km from downtown Chanthaburi, roughly a 40–50 min drive · we recommend driving yourself, because there's no convenient public transport and the final stretch climbs uphill and winds · there's free parking plus a pickup service (for an extra charge).

faq.q: What villas does Phureeya Ville have, and how much do they cost?
faq.a: It's a stay of standalone villas, with around 8 houses holding roughly 30 guests · each has air conditioning, satellite TV, a fridge, a private bathroom with hot water, and a mountain-view balcony · prices often start around ฿1,200/night and up, moving with villa size, the number of guests, and the season · since it's a small place, the most accurate price is best checked with the property directly by phone or Line.

faq.q: Who does Check in Phureeya Ville suit?
faq.a: It's a great fit for couples, families, and groups of friends who want to escape the city for a quiet rest in the mountains on a budget they can manage · you get mountain views, mist, cool air, and the privacy of standalone villas · if you're after a luxury hotel with a swimming pool, a spa, and a location within walking distance of shops in town, a hotel in downtown Chanthaburi may suit you better.

faq.q: Does the property have a swimming pool and Wi-Fi?
faq.a: The property has no swimming pool, because it's a small villa stay that sells the atmosphere of nature above all · as for Wi-Fi/mobile signal, the information from different sources doesn't match, and a signal in a mountain area may not be as strong as in town · if you need stable internet, we recommend asking the property directly before booking.

faq.q: Does Phureeya Ville have food, and is it pet-friendly?
faq.a: There's an on-site restaurant and cafe serving Thai-Asian food and coffee against the mountain views, with breakfast available · real reviews praise the food as tasty and reasonably priced · the property welcomes pets at no extra charge · since it's far from outside restaurants, ask about kitchen hours and order meals ahead of time.

faq.q: When is the best time to stay at Check in Phureeya Ville?
faq.a: The most beautiful time is the cool season (November–February), when the air is cool and morning mist appears often · it's the high season for mountain trips on the Pong Nam Ron–Khao Soi Dao side, with limited availability and higher-than-usual prices, so book ahead · and don't forget to pack warm clothes, because the air in the mountains is far cooler than in town, especially at night.
